literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as governor of Meizhou.
idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he died as governor of Meizhou.

literal: Zirui's wife was Lingxuan's younger sister; when Lingxuan won the Later Sovereign's favor, Zirui was posthumously ennobled as governor of Huaizhou, and his sons likewise all rose to eminent posts.
idiomatic: Zirui's wife was Lu Lingxuan's younger sister. Once Lingxuan won the Later Sovereign's favor, Zirui was posthumously raised to governor of Huaizhou, and his sons, one and all, took eminent posts.

literal: Tongyou, at the end of Wuping, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Gate of Yellow Commissions.
idiomatic: Tongyou, at the end of Wuping, held the post of attendant at the Gate of Yellow Commissions.

literal: Tonghui served as Grand Minister of the Palace Store.
idiomatic: Tonghui served as grand minister of the palace store.

literal: Tongxian served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of Direct Communication.
idiomatic: Tongxian served as attendant-in-ordinary of direct communication.

literal: Yet Tongyou in the end proved a worthy official; in the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Vice Minister of the People's Affairs Bureau in the Masters of Writing, and died as governor of Suizhou.
idiomatic: Tongyou, however, proved a worthy official in the end — under Sui in the Kaihuang era he rose to vice minister of the people's affairs bureau in the Masters of Writing and died as governor of Suizhou.

literal: The historian writes: The Grand Ancestor, holding Jinyang — a land of war-horses where the hegemonic design was destined — drilled troops and trained armies, controlled court authority from afar, and entrusted affairs of the capital with deep reliance.
idiomatic: The historian writes: Gao Huan held Jinyang — land of war-horses, cradle of the hegemonic design — where he drilled troops and trained armies, held court power from afar, and entrusted the capital's affairs to men at great remove.

literal: Sun Teng and the rest alike failed to keep integrity and hold to the Way, to make order and disorder their concern; they amassed goods in heavy exactions and filled ravine and gully.
idiomatic: Sun Teng and the rest alike could not keep their integrity or hold order and disorder as their concern. They taxed without mercy and filled ravine and gully with plunder.

literal: In old days when Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu dwelt at Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?
idiomatic: Long ago Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu held Xudu — were they not utterly unlike this?

literal: It was thanks to Shizong's entry to assist in government, rebuking their arrogance and excess, richly treating Cui Xuan and setting his frost-white censor's brush in motion — otherwise, would the gentlemen have grown sated, and been so easily parted?
idiomatic: Only because Gao Cheng entered to assist, rebuking their arrogance, richly employing Cui Xuan and setting his frost-white censor's brush in motion — otherwise would the court have grown weary of them and been so easily set at odds?

literal: Sun Teng's sincerity in seizing the robe has worth enough to be praised.
idiomatic: Sun Teng's sincerity when he seized Gao Huan's robe — that at least deserves praise.

literal: Longzhi toiled with will and strength in founding Ye; all were men of hidden virtue among the staff, early granted trust, honored in rank and emblem, not falling from court order.
idiomatic: Longzhi toiled in will and strength to found Ye as capital. They were all men of hidden capacity among the staff — early given trust, raised in rank and emblem, not fallen from court order.

literal: Ziru gained his place solely through youthful intimacy and weight of affection — deep bonding and familiar closeness; this was not merit won at the founding, but favor tied in private attachment. No deeds of merit are heard; yet he sat and attained the highest ministry.
idiomatic: Ziru reached power on youthful intimacy alone — deep bonds and familiar warmth, not merit won in founding days, but favor woven in private attachment. No deed of merit is recorded; yet he sat and rose to the highest ministry.

literal: The uncle's love, instructing in right conduct; Yingzhi's bearing and character are weighty; Youzhi's purity and self-reliance — these have worth enough to be named.
idiomatic: The uncle's love that taught right conduct; Yingzhi's bearing worth honoring; Youzhi's purity and self-reliance — these at least deserve mention.

literal: The encomium says: Hong and San drew close as followers; Xiao and Cao lent wing to the throne.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Hong and San drew close as followers; Xiao and Cao lent wing to the throne.

literal: As Qi's fortune rose suddenly, Sun and Gao brought forth their strength.
idiomatic: When Qi's fortune rose in sudden spate, Sun and Gao brought forth their strength.

literal: Gorging on goods without satiety — much to shame their ministerial robes.
idiomatic: Gorging on wealth without end — much to shame the minister's robe.

literal: Sima glib and nimble — clever speech and pleasant looks.
idiomatic: Sima — glib, nimble, clever of tongue and pleasant of face.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
